title: Send: reply to UT Dallas (Edwin Van Der Vlist) — Fall marketing capstone
question: On Yes, I deliver this ready-to-send reply to YOUR inbox for you to send to Edwin (cc Don). Approve?
context: Warm intro from Don Proeschel (UTD Corporate Relations) to Edwin Van Der Vlist, who runs the business-school marketing capstone teams. Origin: your NBC 5 DFW feature. Reply confirms interest, frames the project (sell the open ~135 kg on the early-2027 BLK3 flight, students directing the EXO3 agent fleet), and asks for a team + a call. Full semester scope brief attached to task 1671.
proposedAction:
To: Edwin Van Der Vlist <EdwinVanDerVlist@utdallas.edu>
Cc: Don Proeschel <don.proeschel@utdallas.edu>
Subject: RE: How About a Fall Semester Marketing Project For Exos Aerospace?

Hello Edwin,

Thank you, Don, for the introduction. I would welcome a Fall semester marketing capstone team, and I think we can give your students an unusually good project.

Here is the short version of the client problem. Exos Aerospace is one of only three FAA-licensed reusable rocket launch providers in the United States. We have been flying suborbital vehicles since 2018, and our next flight of BLK3, our precision suborbital reusable launch vehicle, is targeted for early 2027 with roughly 135 kg of payload capacity still open to sell. The capstone challenge is to help us market and sell that payload space.

What makes this different from a normal marketing project is how the team would work. Exos runs an AI-native operating model we call EXO3, an internal fleet of AI agents that already handle research, outreach drafting, and CRM work. The capstone team would sit on top of that stack as the human strategy and creative layer, directing the agents rather than doing all the manual grind themselves. The students learn go-to-market marketing the modern way, humans setting strategy and creative while an agent fleet executes at scale, on a real revenue target. It is a strong story for the business school and, I would think, for your UTDesign showcase.

At a high level a semester could run like this:
- Weeks 1-2: onboard to the EXO3 stack and brand assets, define the ideal payload customer
- Weeks 3-5: segment and size the payload market (university research, defense and government test, in-space startups, sensor and component qualification, education and brand payloads)
- Weeks 5-8: build the campaign, a payload buyer microsite, one-pager, pitch deck, and a social and video series under our SPACEavailable campaign
- Weeks 8-12: run AI-augmented outreach, students author the messaging and creative and the agent fleet personalizes and scales it, all sends approved on our side
- Weeks 12-15: qualify the pipeline, advance the payload manifest for the 2027 flight, and deliver a final presentation and a reusable playbook

We would provide governed access to our tools, brand assets, media, and direct time with me and our BD team. I have put the full project scope in a short brief I can send along once we connect.

Would you have a team available for the fall, and do you have time for a short call this week or next to walk through it? Happy to work around your schedule.

Best regards,

John Quinn
Cofounder & CEO
